title: Your Heart Produces Enough Energy to Drive a Truck
fact: Over a lifetime, your heart produces enough energy to drive a truck to the Moon and back. It beats about 2.5 billion times in an average lifespan.

title: The Sun's Core Reaches 27 Million Degrees Fahrenheit
fact: The core of the Sun reaches temperatures of about 27 million degrees Fahrenheit (15 million°C). This extreme heat enables nuclear fusion.

title: Antarctica Has No Permanent Residents
fact: Antarctica has no permanent human residents, only seasonal researchers. About 1,000-4,000 people live there at any given time, depending on the season.

title: A Group of Flamingos Is Called a Flamboyance
fact: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance, which perfectly matches their colorful appearance. They often stand on one leg to conserve body heat.

title: Blockchain Can Process 100,000 Transactions Per Second
fact: Some blockchain networks can process over 100,000 transactions per second, though most process far fewer. This depends on the specific network architecture.

title: Forests Can Take 100 Years to Mature
fact: Old-growth forests take over 100 years to develop their complex ecosystems. These ancient forests contain the most biodiversity and store the most carbon.

title: The Declaration of the Rights of Man Was in 1789
fact: The Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, adopted in 1789, established principles of liberty, equality, and popular sovereignty in France.

title: Sharks Can Detect Blood From Miles Away
fact: Sharks can detect blood in the water at concentrations as low as 1 part per million, from up to 3 miles away using their highly sensitive sense of smell.

title: The Solar System Is 4.6 Billion Years Old
fact: The solar system formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a giant molecular cloud. The Sun will continue burning for another 5 billion years.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Oxygen Intake
fact: Despite being only 2% of body weight, your brain uses 20% of your oxygen intake. This makes it extremely sensitive to oxygen deprivation.

title: The Sahara Desert Has Sand Dunes Over 1,000 Feet High
fact: Some sand dunes in the Sahara Desert reach heights of over 1,000 feet (300 meters). The tallest recorded dune is about 1,287 feet high.

title: A Group of Porcupines Is Called a Prickle
fact: A group of porcupines is called a prickle. Despite their dangerous quills, porcupines are generally docile and try to avoid confrontation.

title: The First Ransomware Attack Occurred in 1989
fact: The first known ransomware attack occurred in 1989, when Joseph Popp distributed 20,000 floppy disks containing ransomware disguised as AIDS education software.

title: Trees Can Communicate With Each Other
fact: Trees in forests communicate through underground fungal networks called mycorrhizal networks, sharing nutrients and chemical warnings about insect attacks.

title: The French Revolution Ended in 1799
fact: The French Revolution effectively ended in 1799 when Napoleon Bonaparte seized power, establishing the Consulate and later the Empire.

title: Cheetahs Can't Roar
fact: Cheetahs can't roar; they make chirping and yelping sounds instead. Their vocal cords are structured differently from other big cats that can roar.

title: The Largest Known Star Would Engulf Earth's Orbit
fact: If placed at our Sun's position, the star UY Scuti would extend past the orbit of Jupiter, engulfing Earth and Mars.

title: Your Liver Performs 500 Different Functions
fact: The liver performs over 500 essential functions, including filtering blood, producing bile, storing glycogen, and detoxifying harmful substances.

title: The Largest Salt Flat Is in Bolivia
fact: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the world's largest salt flat at 4,086 square miles. During wet season, it becomes the world's largest mirror.

title: Peregrine Falcons Dive at 240 mph
fact: Peregrine falcons are the fastest animals on Earth, diving at speeds up to 240 mph to catch prey in mid-air.

title: WiFi Passwords Originated from Banking
fact: The concept of passwords originated from ancient Roman military watchwords. Modern digital passwords evolved from computer time-sharing systems in the 1960s.

title: Forests Generate Their Own Rainfall
fact: Large forests like the Amazon create their own rainfall systems through transpiration, releasing so much water vapor that it forms clouds and generates rain.

title: The First Written Constitution Was in 1755 BCE
fact: The oldest known written constitution is the Constitution of Medina, established by Prophet Muhammad in 622 CE. However, the US Constitution dates to 1787.

title: A Group of Rhinoceros Is Called a Crash
fact: A group of rhinoceros is called a crash. These endangered animals are threatened by poaching for their horns.

title: Your Body Has More Bacteria Than Human Cells
fact: Your body contains about 38 trillion bacterial cells compared to 30 trillion human cells. These microbes are essential for digestion and immunity.

title: The Amazon River Has 1,100 Tributaries
fact: The Amazon River has over 1,100 tributaries, contributing to its massive flow that represents about 20% of the world's river flow into the ocean.

title: A Group of Hedgehogs Is Called an Array
fact: A group of hedgehogs is called an array. These small mammals have about 5,000-7,000 quills covering their bodies.

title: The Dark Web Contains 7.5 Petabytes of Data
fact: The dark web contains approximately 7.5 petabytes of data, though this number fluctuates. It represents only a small fraction of the total internet.

title: Trees Can Reduce Air Pollution
fact: Trees absorb pollutants like nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide through their leaves. A single tree can remove 0.4-1.5 pounds of pollutants annually.

title: The French Revolution's Reign of Terror Lasted 10 Months
fact: The Reign of Terror (1793-1794) lasted about 10 months, during which about 17,000 people were executed by guillotine.

title: A Group of Stingrays Is Called a Fever
fact: A group of stingrays is called a fever. These graceful swimmers use their disc-shaped bodies to glide through the water.

title: A Photon Takes 100,000 Years to Travel from Sun's Core to Surface
fact: It takes a photon about 100,000 years to travel from the Sun's core to its surface, but only 8 minutes to travel from there to Earth.

title: Your Brain Has a Storage Capacity of 2.5 Petabytes
fact: Your brain's memory storage capacity is estimated at about 2.5 petabytes (2.5 million gigabytes), equivalent to 3 million hours of TV shows.

title: Mount Kilimanjaro Has Three Volcanic Cones
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro has three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, and Shira. Kibo is the highest and could erupt again despite being dormant.

title: A Group of Cheetahs Is Called a Coalition
fact: A group of cheetahs is called a coalition. Male cheetahs often form coalitions to protect their territory and hunting grounds.

title: The First 1 GB Hard Drive Cost $40,000
fact: IBM introduced the first gigabyte-capacity hard drive in 1980. It weighed about 550 pounds and cost $40,000. Today, 1 TB drives cost under $50.

title: Forests Store 45% of All Terrestrial Carbon
fact: Forests store approximately 45% of all carbon stored on land, making them crucial for regulating Earth's climate.

title: The Napoleonic Wars Lasted 12 Years
fact: The Napoleonic Wars (1803-1815) lasted about 12 years and involved most of Europe. Napoleon commanded forces across multiple continents.

title: A Group of Eagles Is Called a Convocation
fact: A group of eagles is called a convocation. Bald eagles mate for life and return to the same nest year after year.

title: The Milky Way Will Collide with Andromeda
fact: The Milky Way and Andromeda galaxies are approaching each other at 250,000 mph and will merge in about 4.5 billion years.

title: Your Stomach Has a pH of 1-3
fact: Your stomach acid has a pH between 1 and 3, making it strong enough to dissolve metal. It protects against pathogens in food.

title: The Driest Place Is in Antarctica
fact: The McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica are the driest places on Earth, with virtually no ice or snow and extremely low humidity.

title: A Group of Jellyfish Is Called a Smack
fact: A group of jellyfish is called a smack. Jellyfish have been floating in Earth's oceans for over 500 million years.

title: Cloud Computing Was Coined in 1996
fact: The term 'cloud computing' was coined in 1996 by Compaq executives. The first widely available cloud services appeared around 2006.

title: Trees Can Live for Thousands of Years
fact: Some bristlecone pine trees have been alive for over 5,000 years, making them the oldest known living organisms on Earth.

title: The Suez Canal Took 10 Years to Build
fact: The Suez Canal took 10 years to build (1859-1869) and is 120 miles long. It connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

title: A Group of Kangaroos Is Called a Mob
fact: A group of kangaroos is called a mob. They use their strong tails for balance when hopping and as a fifth leg when standing.

title: The Universe Contains 2 Trillion Galaxies
fact: The observable universe contains about 2 trillion galaxies, each containing hundreds of billions of stars. Most galaxies are dwarf galaxies.

title: Your Body Has 12 Systems Working Together
fact: The human body has 12 major organ systems: skeletal, muscular, nervous, endocrine, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, immune, and others.

title: The Amazon Contains 16% of World's Freshwater
fact: The Amazon basin contains about 16% of the world's freshwater. The river alone holds more water than the next 10 largest rivers combined.

title: A Group of Badgers Is Called a Cete
fact: A group of badgers is called a cete. Honey badgers are considered the most fearless animals in the world.

title: The First 1 TB Solid-State Drive Costs $1,500
fact: Consumer 1 TB solid-state drives now cost under $100, but early models in 2007 cost around $1,500 for just 32 GB.

title: Forests Cover 4 Billion Hectares
fact: Forests cover approximately 4 billion hectares (9.9 billion acres) of Earth's land surface, though this is decreasing due to deforestation.

title: The Panama Canal Took 10 Years to Build
fact: The Panama Canal took about 10 years to build (1904-1914), though French attempts began in 1881. It is 50 miles long.

title: A Group of Wildebeest Is Called a Cracker
fact: A group of wildebeest is called a cracker. Each year, about 1.5 million wildebeest migrate across the Serengeti in one of Earth's greatest wildlife spectacles.

title: Black Holes Can Sing in B-Flat
fact: In 2003, astronomers detected sound waves from a black hole in the Perseus cluster. The note is B-flat, 57 octaves below middle C.

title: Your Brain Is 60% Fat
fact: Your brain is about 60% fat, making it one of the fattiest organs in the body. This fat is essential for brain cell structure and function.

title: The Great Barrier Reef Has 3,000 Individual Reefs
fact: The Great Barrier Reef consists of about 3,000 individual reef systems and 900 islands, stretching over 1,400 miles along Australia's coast.

title: A Group of Otters Is Called a Romp
fact: A group of otters is called a romp. Sea otters often hold hands while sleeping to avoid drifting apart in the water.

title: The First Computer Mouse Was Invented in 1964
fact: Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in 1964 at Stanford Research Institute. It was made of wood with two wheels.

title: Forests Provide 75% of Urban Freshwater
fact: Forested watersheds provide approximately 75% of the world's accessible fresh water for domestic, agricultural, and industrial use.

title: The Titanic Had 20 Lifeboats but Needed 48
fact: The Titanic carried only 20 lifeboats, enough for about half the passengers. Maritime regulations at the time didn't require more.

title: A Group of Skunks Is Called a Stench
fact: A group of skunks is called a stench. Their spray can be detected by humans from up to 1.5 miles away.

title: The Moon Is Slowly Moving Away
fact: The Moon moves about 3.8 cm away from Earth each year. In 600 million years, total solar eclipses will no longer be possible.

title: Your Brain Weighs About 3 Pounds
fact: An adult brain weighs about 3 pounds (1.4 kg). It contains 86 billion neurons, each connected to thousands of others.

title: The Amazon Has 2.5 Million Insect Species
fact: Scientists estimate the Amazon rainforest contains about 2.5 million insect species, though many remain undiscovered and unnamed.

title: A Group of Crocodiles Is Called a Bask
fact: A group of crocodiles is called a bask. Crocodiles have the strongest bite force of any animal, up to 3,700 PSI.

title: The First Digital Camera Had 0.1 Megapixels
fact: The first commercial digital camera in 1990 had only 0.14 megapixels and cost $10,000. Modern smartphones have cameras with 100+ megapixels.

title: Forests Can Filter 85% of Particulate Matter
fact: Trees and forests can filter up to 85% of particulate matter from the air, significantly improving air quality in urban areas.

title: The Berlin Wall Was 96 Miles Long
fact: The Berlin Wall was about 96 miles long and included over 300 watchtowers. Its construction cut West Berlin off from the surrounding East Germany.

title: A Group of Lizards Is Called a Lounge
fact: A group of lizards is called a lounge. Some lizards can detach their tails to escape predators and then regrow them.

title: Saturn Would Float in Water
fact: Saturn is the least dense planet; if you could find a bathtub big enough, it would float. Its density is less than that of water.

title: Your Body Has 206 Bones
fact: Adults have 206 bones, but babies are born with about 300 that fuse together as they grow. The smallest bone is in the ear.

title: The Amazon Rainforest Has 15,000 Tree Species
fact: Scientists have cataloged at least 15,000 tree species in the Amazon, with many more likely undiscovered in this biodiversity hotspot.

title: A Group of Hippos Is Called a Pod
fact: A group of hippos is called a pod. Despite their cute appearance, hippos are among Africa's most dangerous animals.

title: The First Computer Program Was Written in 1843
fact: Ada Lovelace wrote the first computer program in 1843 for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine. It calculated Bernoulli numbers.

title: Forests Reduce Urban Noise by 50%
fact: Trees and vegetation can reduce urban noise pollution by up to 50% by absorbing and scattering sound waves.

title: The First Moon Landing Cost $25.4 Billion
fact: The Apollo program cost about $25.4 billion (about $180 billion today), representing about 4% of US GDP at its peak.

title: A Group of Parrots Is Called a Pandemonium
fact: A group of parrots is called a pandemonium. Parrots are among the most intelligent birds and can learn to mimic human speech.

title: The Sun's Light Takes 8 Minutes to Reach Earth
fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, traveling at 186,000 miles per second.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Your Calories
fact: Despite being only 2% of body weight, your brain uses about 20% of your caloric intake, making it extremely energy-intensive.

title: The Atacama Desert Has the Clearest Skies
fact: The Atacama Desert in Chile has the clearest skies on Earth, making it ideal for astronomical observatories.

title: A Group of Seals Is Called a Rookery
fact: A group of seals is called a rookery. Seals can hold their breath for up to 2 hours while diving for food.

title: The First WiFi Network Operated in 1997
fact: The first WiFi standard (802.11) was released in 1997, enabling wireless data transfer at 2 Mbps. Modern WiFi can reach 10+ Gbps.

title: Forests Produce 50% of Earth's Oxygen
fact: Forests and phytoplankton together produce about 50% of Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis.

title: The Suez Canal Opened in 1869
fact: The Suez Canal opened on November 17, 1869, after 10 years of construction. It revolutionized global trade by connecting Europe and Asia.

title: A Group of Leopards Is Called a Leap
fact: A group of leopards is called a leap. Leopards are the most widespread of all big cats, found across Africa and Asia.

title: The Sun's Diameter Is 109 Times Earth's
fact: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times that of Earth. About 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun.

title: Your Heart Beats 100,000 Times Per Day
fact: Your heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood. This adds up to about 3 billion beats in a lifetime.

title: The Amazon Rainforest Gets 9 Feet of Rain Annually
fact: The Amazon rainforest receives about 9 feet (2.7 meters) of rainfall per year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

title: A Group of Baboons Is Called a Troop
fact: A group of baboons is called a troop. Baboons live in complex social hierarchies with clear dominance structures.

title: The First Bitcoin Transaction Was in 2009
fact: The first Bitcoin transaction occurred on January 12, 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto sent 10 BTC to Hal Finney.

title: Trees Can Absorb 48 Pounds of CO2 Per Year
fact: A single mature tree can absorb about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year and release enough oxygen for two people to breathe.

title: The Panama Canal Opened in 1914
fact: The Panama Canal opened on August 15, 1914, after a decade of construction. It handles over 12,000 ships annually.

title: A Group of Foxes Is Called a Skulk
fact: A group of foxes is called a skulk. Red foxes can hear a mouse squeak from 100 feet away.

title: The Moon Has 181 Giant Craters
fact: The Moon has at least 181 giant craters over 12 miles wide. The largest is the South Pole-Aitken basin, 1,600 miles across.

title: Your Lungs Have 300 Million Alveoli
fact: Your lungs contain about 300 million tiny air sacs called alveoli. If spread flat, they'd cover about 70 square meters.

title: Lake Superior Has 78.6 Trillion Gallons of Water
fact: Lake Superior contains about 78.6 trillion gallons of water, enough to cover North and South America in 1 foot of water.

title: A Group of Iguanas Is Called a Massacre
fact: A group of iguanas is called a massacre. Marine iguanas from the Galapagos are the only seagoing lizards.
